structured_output.situation_summary: New, insidious-onset exertional dyspnea with a dry cough emerging in the early ADC-047 exposure window (C1D15). The most likely working explanations right now are: Early drug-induced ILD / pneumonitis (DXd-class signature DLT); Tumor progression of metastatic NSCLC; Deconditioning / treatment-related fatigue; Infection or anemia.
structured_output.physician_note: This is not acute respiratory failure right now, but it does fit the early pattern of DXd-class lung toxicity that needs active tracking; any further oxygen drop or fever should trigger a lower threshold to escalate.
immediate_actions: Start tracking resting and post-activity oxygen, heart rate, temperature, cough frequency, and whether the same walking distance feels harder.
Keep activity slower for the next few days and avoid stairs, brisk walking, or anything that clearly provokes dyspnea.
If oxygen falls below 92%, or resting shortness of breath, fever, or chest pain appears, contact the trial team or emergency care immediately.

Use an ADC-friendly eating pattern right away: small frequent bland higher-protein meals; if diarrhea is present, add oral rehydration solution or lightly salted rice broth; if nausea is strong, move larger liquids and soups to at least 30 minutes before or after meals.

monitoring_plan.what_to_monitor: Resting/post-activity oxygen, temperature, cough frequency, walking tolerance, and whether dyspnea shifts to rest
monitoring_plan.frequency: At least morning and evening daily, plus an extra check after exertion
monitoring_plan.next_checkin: Trial-team review within 24 hours, with HRCT-directed escalation if symptoms progress

structured_output.nearest_care_instructions: SpO2 < 92%, resting dyspnea, fever, or chest pain - contact the trial team immediately.
structured_output.guardrail: This page is a patient-facing summary for a clinical-trial safety review scenario. It supports next-step understanding but does not replace emergency care or formal medical judgment.
